hook_text: They call me Big John. I taught a Grade 5 student Grade 12 maths. And she passed. Let me show you how.
clip_script:
They call me Big John. I taught a Grade 5 student Grade 12 maths. And she passed. Let me show you how.

Imagine you have a little snowball at the top of a snowy hill. You roll it down. As it rolls, it picks up snow.

But here is the trick: as it gets bigger, the new snow it picks up also picks up more snow. The snowball doesn't just grow; the growth grows.

That is compound growth in maths. It's growth on top of growth. It's making your money work for you, and then making the new money work for you too.

Don't rush to try and memorize a complicated formula. Start with the logic. Start with the snowball. If you can understand that, you can pass Grade 12 maths.
